title: Roman numerals
summary: A small library that converts integers to Roman numerals and back, in the standard subtractive notation, from 1 to 3999.

requirements.title: Write a Roman numeral
requirements.description: romannum.to_roman(n: int) -> str returns the numeral in upper case, subtractive notation (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM).

criteria.then: it returns I, IV, XLII, MCMXCIV and MMMCMXCIX

criteria.given: an integer outside 1 to 3999, such as 0, -1 or 4000

requirements.title: Read a Roman numeral
requirements.description: romannum.from_roman(s: str) -> int reads a numeral written in upper case, standard notation.

criteria.given: the numerals I, IV, XLII, MCMXCIV and MMMCMXCIX
a text that is not a numeral in standard notation, such as IIII, IC, ABC or an empty text

requirements.title: Convert both ways without loss
requirements.description: Writing a number and reading it back gives the number again.

criteria.when: it is written with to_roman and read back with from_roman
criteria.then: the result is the integer itself

quality.target: converting all 3999 numbers both ways takes under 1 second

constraints: Python 3.11 or later, standard library only.
The package is romannum/ at the project root: romannum/__init__.py defines to_roman and from_roman.
Tests live in tests/ and run with pytest from the project root.
